title: Vinorelbine and cisplatin · 28-day cycle
purpose: After surgery, treatment aims to lower the chance of cancer returning. For advanced or recurrent lung cancer, it aims to control disease and symptoms. Your team should mark which goal applies to you; benefit is not guaranteed.

agents.name: Vinorelbine
agents.mechanism: Disrupts microtubules needed for cell division
agents.explanation: Vinorelbine disrupts the cell structures that help divide chromosomes. This can slow cancer growth and also affect blood cells, nerves and the bowel.
agents.watch: Report fever, constipation, numbness or pain at the infusion site promptly.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

phases.label: Chemotherapy
phases.detail: A cycle lasts 28 days (4 weeks). Vinorelbine is given on Days 1, 8, 15, 22. Cisplatin is given on Days 1 and 8. Four cycles are planned, with review before doses. Delays or omitted doses may be needed for safety.

phases.label: Review after chemotherapy
phases.detail: Scans and follow-up depend on the treatment goal. Surgery or radiotherapy is not automatically part of this regimen; ask where any separately planned treatment fits.

timeline.label: Vinorelbine visits
timeline.text: Days 1, 8, 15, 22 only; not a continuous infusion.

timeline.label: Watch for symptoms every day
timeline.text: Blood counts and symptoms vary; the calendar cannot predict a safe day.

support.title: Prevent and manage sickness
support.text: Follow your prescribed anti-sickness and constipation-prevention plan. Cisplatin days need kidney-protecting fluids and electrolyte checks. Do not repeat the full cisplatin anti-sickness course on a vinorelbine-only day unless prescribed.

support.title: Bowel care
support.text: Take the prescribed laxative plan. Tell the team if your bowels slow down; severe pain, swelling or vomiting needs urgent advice.

support.title: Protect kidneys, hearing and nerves
support.text: Follow your individual drinking advice and report reduced urine, ringing ears, hearing changes or tingling. Ask before taking new medicines or supplements.

questions.a: After surgery, treatment aims to lower the chance of cancer returning. For advanced or recurrent lung cancer, it aims to control disease and symptoms. Your team should mark which goal applies to you; benefit is not guaranteed.

questions.q: What if a weekly dose is missed?
questions.a: The team decides whether to omit, delay or change a dose. Do not add a missed dose yourself; the two vinorelbine/cisplatin schedules have different rules.
It is not built into this chemotherapy schedule. Ask your team to explain any separately planned radiotherapy or other treatment.

context_label: Postoperative adjuvant or advanced/recurrent NSCLC: confirm your treatment goal
schedule_summary: A cycle lasts 28 days (4 weeks). Vinorelbine is given on Days 1, 8, 15, 22. Cisplatin is given on Days 1 and 8. Four cycles are planned, with review before doses. Delays or omitted doses may be needed for safety.
administration_text: Vinorelbine is infused over15 minutes, followed by a saline flush. Cisplatin is infused over about one hour on its treatment days, with fluids before and afterwards. Checks, preparation and support medicines make the appointment longer than the infusion itself.
monitoring_summary: Blood count every week; kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Report hearing changes, tingling, bowel problems and poor fluid intake before every dose. Extra tests and scans follow your individual plan.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team immediately for fever or sudden illness, shaking chills, breathing difficulty, chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine, severe abdominal pain or constipation with vomiting. Tell the nurse immediately about burning or pain at the infusion site. Do not wait until the next visit.
consent_support: Follow your prescribed anti-sickness and constipation-prevention plan. Cisplatin days need kidney-protecting fluids and electrolyte checks. Do not repeat the full cisplatin anti-sickness course on a vinorelbine-only day unless prescribed. Discuss serious infection, hearing or nerve damage that can persist, kidney injury, fertility and rare life-threatening effects.

chronology_notes.title: A schedule, not a prediction
chronology_notes.text: Symptoms may occur on any day. Treatment depends on blood results and how you are feeling.

chronology_notes.title: Your overall plan
chronology_notes.text: Four cycles take approximately 16 weeks if there are no delays. Confirm the intended goal, number of cycles and any separate local treatment.

timeline_note: Calendar shows planned visits only. No patient dates are required.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for fever or sudden illness, shaking chills, breathing difficulty, chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine, severe abdominal pain or constipation with vomiting. Tell the nurse immediately about burning or pain at the infusion site. Do not wait until the next visit.
passport_visit_note: Use one group per cycle; record actual doses, delays and symptoms with your team.
anatomy: Report ringing ears, hearing change, numbness or weakness; effects can persist.
Report mouth sores that make eating or drinking difficult.
Fluids protect kidneys; call for very little urine or inability to drink.
Constipation and nausea need early treatment; severe pain or vomiting needs urgent advice.
Fever or sudden illness needs immediate advice. Tell the nurse about infusion pain.

monitoring_schedule.note: Relative stages, not equal time intervals. There is no routine heart-scan schedule in this regimen.

sections.title: Before the visit

sections.title: Time in the unit
sections.text: Vinorelbine is infused over15 minutes, followed by a saline flush. Cisplatin is infused over about one hour on its treatment days, with fluids before and afterwards. Checks, preparation and support medicines make the appointment longer than the infusion itself.

sections.title: IV access
sections.text: Suitable IV access is required. No routine take-home pump. Tell the nurse promptly about pain or burning.

sections.title: Home support
sections.text: Follow your prescribed anti-sickness and constipation-prevention plan. Cisplatin days need kidney-protecting fluids and electrolyte checks. Do not repeat the full cisplatin anti-sickness course on a vinorelbine-only day unless prescribed.

sections.title: After the course
sections.text: Agree follow-up, scans and how to report persistent problems.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.summary: Trials support cisplatin-based chemotherapy after surgery for selected lung cancers. The benefit depends on the stage and treatment goal; evidence after surgery cannot be used as a prognosis for advanced cancer.
evidence.intro: Trials support cisplatin-based chemotherapy after surgery for selected lung cancers. The benefit depends on the stage and treatment goal; evidence after surgery cannot be used as a prognosis for advanced cancer.
evidence.interpretation: JBR.10 studied resected stage IB/II disease. Its schedule matches the 28-day split cisplatin regimen more closely. No individual survival estimate or metastatic benefit percentage is provided here.
evidence.caveat: JBR.10 studied resected stage IB/II disease. Its schedule matches the 28-day split cisplatin regimen more closely. No individual survival estimate or metastatic benefit percentage is provided here.

chapters.title: Your treatment and its aim
chapters.intro: After surgery, treatment aims to lower the chance of cancer returning. For advanced or recurrent lung cancer, it aims to control disease and symptoms. Your team should mark which goal applies to you; benefit is not guaranteed.

items.title: Why two medicines?
items.text: The medicines interfere with cancer-cell division in different ways. They can also affect healthy cells.

items.title: Choosing treatment
items.text: Discuss likely benefit, side effects, alternatives and what matters most to you.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: Trials support cisplatin-based chemotherapy after surgery for selected lung cancers. The benefit depends on the stage and treatment goal; evidence after surgery cannot be used as a prognosis for advanced cancer. JBR.10 studied resected stage IB/II disease. Its schedule matches the 28-day split cisplatin regimen more closely. No individual survival estimate or metastatic benefit percentage is provided here.

chapters.intro: Call your oncology team immediately for fever or sudden illness, shaking chills, breathing difficulty, chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine, severe abdominal pain or constipation with vomiting. Tell the nurse immediately about burning or pain at the infusion site. Do not wait until the next visit.

items.title: Infection
items.text: Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness can be serious even between visits.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Report constipation early; severe pain or vomiting needs urgent advice.

items.title: Hearing and nerves
items.text: Tell the team promptly about hearing changes, ringing ears, tingling or weakness.

chapters.title: Everyday life
chapters.intro: Adjust activity and support to how you feel.

items.title: Food and fluids
items.text: Ask for help with poor appetite or sickness. Follow individual hydration advice, including any fluid restriction.

items.title: Medicines and pregnancy
items.text: Check medicines and supplements with the team. Discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding before treatment.

chapters.title: After chemotherapy
chapters.intro: Your next plan depends on why treatment was given.

items.title: Other treatments
items.text: Surgery and radiotherapy require separate plans; neither is automatically added by this schedule.

items.title: Ongoing effects
items.text: Report persistent hearing or nerve changes and attend kidney/blood checks as arranged.
